<description>
The first commit adds `p2p_1p1c_liveness`, an end-to-end fuzz target for parent and child relay. It
  drives a real PeerManager with real messages and validation, and checks that if an honest peer announces
  the child of an acceptable parent and child, the child reaches the mempool within a bounded time,
  whatever other peers do. Known liveness holes are marked in the target as flags that turn the check off
  once opened, including this one. With that flag turned off, the target finds this bug on master from an
  empty corpus in under an hour on one core; an earlier version found it first
  (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36371#issuecomment-5937814761).

  The second commit hands reconsideration over to a remaining announcer when the marked announcement is
  erased, and removes the flag.

Follow-up PR to fill the holes is here: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36506
</description>

[2026-10-25] c:6395056559 comment by fametrano (contributor):
tACK 65b48ba1f1f4c6c04a0d1bea9f7774091ec4e130

I reproduced the hole end to end with a Boost case of my own. Peer A sends twelve children and peer B announces each of them by wtxid, so each orphan has two announcers. A then sends the parent and disconnects before its next turn, and B runs until it has no more work. On master 6 of the 12 children reach the mempool, and the other 6 stay in the orphanage with nobody to reconsider them. With this PR all 12 are accepted in 13 turns of B, and the orphanage is empty. The updated `peer_worksets` case fails on master at its new hand-over checks and passes here.

The hand-over keeps the callers' iterators valid. `EraseForPeer`, `EraseTxInternal` and `LimitOrphans` advance their iterator before each erase. In `Erase()`, `lower_bound` can land on the announcement being erased, and the `++` skips it. `modify()` only changes the other announcement's `m_reconsider`, which moves it within `ByPeer` alone, and that key stays unique through `m_entry_sequence`.

I tested the head merged into master a773e1e33b, in a Debug build, with the orphanage, denialofservice and txdownload unit tests, p2p_orphan_handling and p2p_opportunistic_1p1c. Under libFuzzer, p2p_1p1c_liveness ran for 10 minutes and txorphanage_sim for 3, with no crash. I repeated all of it with #36594 and #36578 merged on top, with the liveness target for 5 minutes and txorphanage_sim for 1. I can share the test case as a gist.
</new_statements>
